    <div class="ms-meta-row">

  <div class="ms-body">

    <div class="ms-main">

      <p class="ms-desc">Since September 2024 I have been working as a Climate Scientist for Tragsatec, providing climate services to Spain's national meteorological agency (AEMET). The work sits at the intersection of statistical climatology, geospatial analysis, and data communication — translating complex seasonal forecast products into accessible, interactive tools for decision-makers and the public.</p>

      <p class="ms-desc">Seasonal forecasting operates on timescales of one to six months ahead, using statistical post-processing techniques to calibrate the output of global climate models against observed data. The challenge is not only scientific — it is also communicative. A seasonal forecast is only useful if the people who need it can understand and act on it.</p>

      <div class="ms-callout">
        <p>This project is the one where I have pushed furthest into data communication and interactive visualisation. Building dashboards in Plotly, Dash and Shiny, writing D3.js components, and working with Datawrapper for public-facing outputs has changed how I think about the relationship between climate data and the people who need it.</p>
      </div>

      <h2 class="ms-subtitle">What I do</h2>
      <ul class="ms-list">
        <li>Seasonal forecasting and statistical post-processing of global climate model output</li>
        <li>Geospatial analysis of climate variables across the Spanish territory</li>
        <li>Interactive dashboard development with Plotly, Dash and Shiny</li>
        <li>Data visualisation for public and institutional audiences using D3.js and Datawrapper</li>
        <li>Workflow automation and batch processing in HPC environments using Bash</li>
      </ul>

        <span>Geospatial analysis</span>
      </div>
